summary: TASK-070 (REQ-104 dead-code / shell-capability deletion), independent FOURTH-round review of candidate 9086e04c, focused on the three comment fixes this round claims (F-r3-1 sync/mod.rs header, F-r3-2 sync_e2e.rs line-77 comment, F-r3-3 sync_e2e.rs header backoff attribution) and on whether the new wording introduces yet another inaccuracy. I did not write any of this code. I re-bound the candidate myself (all 157 candidate_files sha256 match the worktree, 0 mismatched/missing; the 17 modified non-.workflow-kit files are all inside allowed_paths; no untracked file outside .workflow-kit), re-ran three of the four gates (cargo test exit 0 = 27 suites / 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored, matching the record and the baseline; npm run lint exit 0 = 0 warnings/0 errors; npm run test:frontend exit 0 = 26/26 + 277/277 = 303/303) and read the recorded build log (exit 0, empty stderr); I also ran tsc -b (the typecheck half of the build gate) exit 0. F-r3-1 is genuinely fixed: the false 'never implemented' absolute is gone and every historical clause now checks out against git (9828c8f sync.rs pull_entries calls db::feeds_fetch_failed inside a failed_feeds loop; 51dc66e keeps it via feeds_fetch_failed_bound; 0ba940f^ still has 'let (since_s, miniflux_feeds, failed_feeds)' and 'for feed in &failed_feeds', while 0ba940f itself deletes both lines and leaves zero feeds_fetch_failed references in sync.rs). F-r3-2 is genuinely fixed: I instrumented the test and dumped the database immediately after sync 1 - articles are [(1, feed 1, direct), (2, feed 2, miniflux, url=http://example.com/only-remote)] and feeds.feed_url = 'http://example.com/remote-only.xml' has remote_id = 11, i.e. the entry IS created in that round by the rule the new comment names (sync/entries.rs:145-151 upserts an unmatched remote entry when maps.feed_mf_to_id has its remote feed). F-r3-3 is genuinely fixed: the header no longer attributes backoff to fetch_failed, and the fail_count/next_retry_at mechanism, the set_feed_fetch_state writer, the feeds_due_for_refresh filter and the FeedRow -> list_feeds -> api.ts fetchFailed -> Sidebar feed-error-dot marker path all verify; the two headers are now mutually consistent. I also re-confirmed the substance: all nine deletions had zero production call sites at HEAD (checked with git grep against HEAD, not only the worktree), zero residue of fallback_entries / syncNow / STATE_FILE_NAME, no new dead_code/unused warnings (warning multisets of baseline and this candidate are identical, 14 lines each), no dependency-file change, LF endings on all 17 changed files, the real user database untouched, and no assertion altered (18 assert macros on both sides of sync_e2e.rs). I found no new false clause this round; the one clause I probed hardest ('本文件后续断言即以此为据') is true of the rule it names, and I recorded the nuance in the maintainability check. Verdict: PASS.

review_checks.analysis: Item by item against the seven acceptance criteria. (1) Nine deletions verified zero production call sites against HEAD (git grep <sym> HEAD -- src-tauri/src src src-tauri/tests tools), not just the worktree: feeds_fetch_failed / feeds_fetch_failed_bound / feeds_origin_remote appear only as definitions plus the db.rs pub use; ingestion's non-staged refresh_feed has no caller (production goes through commands/articles.rs:209 and scheduler.rs:147 -> refresh_feed_staged); GReaderClient ::mark_all_read / ::subscribe have zero '.mark_all_read(' / '.subscribe(' call sites; the five superseded sync_map queries appear only as definitions, the re-export and test references; SyncReport.fallback_entries had no increment anywhere (only the two mutually-copying assignments); STATE_FILE_NAME had no reference; api.syncNow had no caller; AiEvent::Error was constructed only by its own test. (2) No new dead_code/unused warnings: I normalised the warning lines of the baseline run (RUN-5380e8e4) and this candidate's recorded run - both are 14 lines, differing only in which per-test target is credited with a duplicate (a scheduling artifact); no warning mentions any deleted item. (3) Four gates green: the recorded cargo_test stdout aggregates to exactly 27 suites / 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored, lint stdout is 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors' with a 0-byte stderr, build stdout ends in a completed Vite build with exit 0 and a 0-byte stderr, and frontend stdout ends in 26/26, 277/277, 303/303 with zero 'failed'/'FAIL' occurrences. (4) Zero residue: git grep for fallback_entries, syncNow and STATE_FILE_NAME over src, src-tauri/src, src-tauri/tests and tools returns nothing, as does the string 'fluxreader-article-state'; the SQL 'WHERE fetch_failed = 1' no longer exists anywhere in src or src-tauri. (5) The sync/mod.rs header no longer claims a nonexistent fallback and now states '该路径在当前实现中已不存在' with the true history; criterion ⑤ is met. (6) No new dependencies: package.json, package-lock.json, src-tauri/Cargo.toml and src-tauri/Cargo.lock are absent from git diff. (7) All 17 changed files are LF-only (crlf=0) with no BOM; the real user database (C:\Users\A\AppData\Roaming\com.fluxreader.app\fluxreader.db, 90112 B) still carries its pre-task mtime 2026-09-19 01:58:09, earlier than the task start (2026-09-20T03:38Z) and than all verification runs, and the tests open only temp-dir databases. Criterion ④ (AiEvent::Error) is handled as 'delete' and truthfully recorded; the retained frontend 'error' branch is documented as a defensive fallback and is still referenced (tsc -b exit 0 under noUnusedParameters). Criterion ⑦: the retired assertions' objects disappeared with the deletion, and the adapted ones were moved onto surviving production entries (sync_match_maps), which I re-verified by mutation (see regression).

I read the actual gate commands, their raw stdout/stderr and re-ran three gates plus the typecheck half of the fourth. cargo_test: the recorded stdout has 27 'test result:' lines aggregating to exactly 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored; my own run reproduces 27 suites / 177 / 0 / 9 with exit 0 and per-suite pass counts identical to the record; the recorded stderr is composed solely of pre-existing mock_greader dead_code notes and a linker-message note, and its normalised warning multiset is IDENTICAL to the baseline run's (14 lines each; the only difference is which test target is credited with a shared duplicate warning). lint: recorded 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors' exit 0; my run reproduces it. frontend: recorded 26/26 + 277/277 = 303/303 with exit 0; my run reproduces 303/303 exit 0. build: not re-run (Vite child process is blocked in this sandbox, per instruction); I read the recorded stdout - a completed production build with exit 0 and a 0-byte stderr - and independently ran its typecheck half tsc -b (exit 0). Assertions were not altered: sync_e2e.rs has 18 assert macros on both sides of the change, and a token-level diff of every changed file (comments and string literals stripped) shows the only sync_e2e differences are the removed fallback_entries println, the renamed local fallback->ingested and the reworded assert message - no predicate, SQL literal or expected value changed. The other counts are consistent with the declared test_review: commands/ai.rs 5->3 (the two retired AiEvent::Error assertions), sync_content_e2e.rs 15->15 (assert! -> assert_eq! tightening), account_lifecycle_e2e.rs 28->28 (set_folder_remote_id replaced by the equivalent SQL write), dedup_sync_e2e.rs 14->15 (the disclosed ADD of the maps-input completeness assertion). The adapted tests still have teeth: the r3 round proved by mutation that forcing a None feed component into id_to_mf_pair makes dedup_sync_e2e::cross_feed_remote_entry_cannot_write_state_or_steal_binding fail, and I independently reproduced the mutation the sync_e2e.rs header now cites - removing only the db::set_feed_fetch_state(..., true, ...) call leaves the suite green and still ingests the bound feed's remote entry, so the header's stated real trigger (the remote_id binding, not the failure flag) is correct. Each mutation was made on a backed-up file and restored byte-identically (sync_e2e.rs sha256 b6e4557762daa6f0d700ebceac65e2d51a0b9351938db2e5ed583a9e07345e44 before and after); afterwards all 157 candidate hashes re-match with 0 mismatches and git status shows no untracked file outside .workflow-kit.

For a deletion task I looked specifically for runtime-reachable residue, including references a plain symbol grep could miss. (a) String / IPC level: the removed frontend method api.syncNow was the only sender of the 'sync_now' invoke name - git grep now finds no 'syncNow' and no inv('sync_now') anywhere in src or tools (the only live sync entry points are inv('sync_phase') at api.ts:491 and inv('refresh_feed') at api.ts:220, both untouched) - while the Rust command commands::sync_now remains registered (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:258) and functional because this task changed its body to delegate to sync::sync_now with identical semantics (feeds_phase then states_phase(full=true), same pushed_states/pulled_entries/errors merge), so no IPC surface was orphaned. (b) Serialized field names: 'fallback_entries' was removed from the Rust struct, the TypeScript interface and the frontend regression harness mock in the same change and no reader remains, so there is no 'reads undefined' path; the retained AiEvent tags 'delta'/'done' are byte-identical and the never-emitted 'error' tag was dropped from the emitter while the receiver branch was kept, so a stray/unknown channel message still surfaces an error instead of being silently discarded (the store's onError callback at src/store/slices/ai.ts:284-294 is still reachable and used). (c) Database columns read elsewhere: the deletion removed Rust query helpers, not schema - feeds.fetch_failed still exists (db/migrations.rs), is still written by set_feed_fetch_state (db/feeds.rs:125) and is still read through FeedRow (which derives Serialize and carries the field), handed out by the list_feeds command (commands/folders.rs:103-105, registered at lib.rs:230), typed at src/lib/api.ts:57, mapped to fetchFailed at api.ts:534 and consumed by the sidebar badge at src/components/Sidebar.tsx:240-247; migrations are untouched, so existing databases stay compatible. The now-deleted query helpers were the only remaining SQL that filtered on that column, and nothing replaced them, so no rarely-exercised branch lost its reader silently. (d) Rarely-exercised branches: the mock's ac=='subscribe' arm was removed because its only producer (GReaderClient::subscribe) was deleted; production emits only ac=unsubscribe / ac=edit (src-tauri/src/greader.rs:510/525) and subscription recording still happens in the quickadd branch and via subscription_edits before the match, so the remaining consumers of subscribed_urls (account_lifecycle_e2e.rs:491, sync_gap_repro_e2e.rs:1185) are intact. (e) One probing detail, disclosed rather than hidden: I removed the second server.add_entry (feed 11, only-remote) and the whole suite still passed (1 passed, with a printed sentinel proving the mutated source was the one compiled) - i.e. no assertion in this file depends on that particular entry. That is a pre-existing coverage observation, not a defect of this task (no assertion was weakened, and the file's source='miniflux' ingestion rule is asserted by the ③ section at sync_e2e.rs:207-219), and the new line-77 comment does not claim otherwise: what it says is that the entry is ingested by that rule and that the file's later assertions rest on it, which holds for the rule.

This round's entire deliverable is comment honesty, so I judged every rewritten clause strictly, in both directions. F-r3-1 (sync/mod.rs header) - clause by clause: '该路径在当前实现中已不存在' is present-tense and true; '它**曾经存在**：Miniflux 协议时期 pull 里有 failed_feeds 循环，直接调 feeds_fetch_failed / feeds_fetch_failed_bound' is confirmed by git (git show 9828c8f:src-tauri/src/sync.rs has 'let failed_feeds = db::feeds_fetch_failed(conn)' and 'for feed in &failed_feeds' inside pull_entries; 51dc66e:src-tauri/src/sync.rs has the same loop fed by db::feeds_fetch_failed_bound inside pull_entries); '0ba940f（协议切换 Google Reader）删掉了该循环' is confirmed both ways (0ba940f^:src-tauri/src/sync.rs still contains both lines, while 0ba940f:src-tauri/src/sync.rs contains zero 'feeds_fetch_failed' and zero 'failed_feeds' references); '此后 feeds.fetch_failed 在 Rust 侧没有读取方' matches the tree (the column is only written, selected into FeedRow and re-serialized - no Rust branch reads it); '这两条查询也随本任务作为死代码删除' is this task's actual change; '该列的现存用途是经 FeedRow（commands/folders.rs 的 list_feeds）下发前端做失败标记（api.ts 的 fetchFailed → Sidebar 的 feed-error-dot）' verifies end to end; '抓取退避由 fail_count / next_retry_at 承担（set_feed_fetch_state 写入、feeds_due_for_refresh 按 next_retry_at 过滤），与该列无关' matches db/feeds.rs:123-138 and :151-157 exactly, and set_feed_fetch_state is the only writer of both columns. No false historical absolute remains (the r2 '从未实现' wording is gone) and no clause over-claims. F-r3-2 (sync_e2e.rs line 77) - the false 'not created this round / no URL match' claim is gone; the replacement names the real rule and I confirmed it empirically: with the test instrumented to dump the database right after sync 1, articles are [(1, feed 1, 'Local Article', direct), (2, feed 2, 'Remote only article', miniflux, url=http://example.com/only-remote)] and feeds 'http://example.com/remote-only.xml' has remote_id = 11, matching the suite's own assertions at lines 122-123 and the code at src-tauri/src/sync/entries.rs:145-151 (an unmatched remote entry is upserted only when maps.feed_mf_to_id holds its remote feed, which the same round's pull_feeds bound). I also probed the trailing clause '本文件后续断言即以此为据' by mutation (removing that add_entry leaves the suite green) - read as a claim about the described rule it is true, because the file's source='miniflux' assertion at lines 207-219 rests on exactly that rule; read as a claim that a later assertion depends on that one entry it would not hold, so I record the mutation here rather than let it pass unnoticed. The file header's mutation citation ('删掉失败标记调用，本套件仍全绿且条目照常入库') also reproduces: I deleted only that set_feed_fetch_state call and the suite stayed green with the entries ingested. F-r3-3 (sync_e2e.rs header) - 'feeds.fetch_failed 在 Rust 侧没有读取方' is true; backoff is attributed to fail_count / next_retry_at with the correct writer and filter, and is no longer listed as a use of fetch_failed; '该列现存用途是下发前端做失败标记' is true; the two headers are now mutually consistent (both say '在 Rust 侧没有读取方' and both credit fail_count / next_retry_at). Re-scan for other contradictions in the touched files: no stale 'Miniflux 兜底' claim survives in any file this task changed (remaining '兜底' hits are unrelated meanings - default folder, favicon, dedup key, extract cover, URL-match fallback, AI defensive branch - and the sync_e2e.rs:232 note explicitly disambiguates the URL-match '兜底' from the Miniflux one); ingestion.rs:1-7 states the retired claim in the present tense and does not repeat the 'never implemented' error; db/sync_map.rs, commands/ai.rs, commands/sync.rs, mock_greader.rs and get_first_folder_id carry the accurate notes verified in earlier rounds. Two residual staleness spots exist but are OUTSIDE this task's allowed_paths and were recorded for a later batch, so they are not defects of this candidate: src/types.ts:44/:70 ('失败走 Miniflux 兜底 + 退避重试' and the source='miniflux' description; the allowed_paths entry 'src/lib/types.ts' does not exist, so the real file is out of scope) and src-tauri/tests/staged_refresh_e2e.rs:195 plus sync_phases_e2e.rs:246 (stale '供 UI 与 Miniflux 兜底查询' wording); the in-scope sync_content_e2e.rs header still names the pre-rename helper names in its coverage list, but that header is not part of this round's deliverable and its coverage statements remain true of the suite's content.

Genuinely not applicable to this change, with a concrete reason instead of an invented benchmark. This task is a pure deletion plus one equivalent delegation, and this round touched only comment text in two files (a per-hunk comparison of the r3 and r4 cumulative-diff artifacts shows the r3->r4 delta is limited to the sync/mod.rs and sync_e2e.rs comment blocks and the artifact's own narrative header - no assertion, setup call, SQL literal or expected value changed). (1) Everything deleted had zero call sites, so none of it executed at runtime: the three Miniflux-era fallback queries, the old non-staged ingestion::refresh_feed, GReaderClient::mark_all_read / subscribe, the five superseded per-item sync_map queries, STATE_FILE_NAME and api.syncNow. (2) The structure that determines sync cost is untouched: sync_match_maps still issues the same fixed set of batch queries and the merge loop still performs O(1) HashMap/HashSet lookups (db/sync_map.rs:47-122, consumed at sync/entries.rs:99-154), so query count and per-entry work are unchanged. (3) The only executed-code change in the whole task, commands::sync_now delegating to sync::sync_now, preserves the sequence feeds_phase (push_feeds + pull_feeds) then states_phase(full=true) and the same error-merge arithmetic (sync/phases.rs:82-92); the single removed operation is one O(1) copy of the deleted fallback_entries counter - nanoseconds against network I/O and SQLite work. (4) The task's quality-goal performance targets (ten-thousand-item startup, layout switching, social-layout article loading) belong to REQ-001/003 and are not on this deletion surface; no workload, baseline or measurement exists for them here, so I fabricated none and claim no speedup.
